item.text: The public tests show the feature is about staging non-empty bytes, handing them off so the same bytes come back, and guaranteeing no leftover files across both success and injected failures. I’m reading the fixture contracts now to see the exact workspace operations and fault model.

The fixture exposes only create, permissions, read, and remove. Because creation observes the file immediately for every allowed actor, the implementation needs to stage under the producer identity first, then explicitly switch visibility to the consumer for handoff, with cleanup in a `finally`.

I’ve made the service stage privately, inject the requested failures at the relevant phases, hand off by changing permissions to the consumer, and remove the staging file in all paths. I’m running the public checks now.

- Hands off intentionally to `consumer`.

- Cleans up on success and on `create`, `write`, `handoff`, and `read` failures.
